text:
ScarlettPort

 A bring-your-own-copy compatibility layer for Xbox Series X S titles on Windows. 
No emulator, no streaming. The title's own x64 code runs on your CPU, and its RDNA2 GPU code is recompiled for your graphics card on the fly. You supply a dump of your own legally purchased copy; nothing of any title is included here. Wine and Proton are the spirit of it.

 Where it stands

Developed and tested so far against one open-world title. It boots, gets through the menus, saves and legal screens, reaches the world and starts gameplay: about 5 fps in the cell scene and about 4 fps while moving on an RTX 3060 (Series S profile), with stable frame pacing. The yard stutter is fixed; the lighting is wrong (ray tracing is off) and first runs freeze on pipeline compiles while moving, so it is not yet verified playable .

 

 

 boots ✅ → intro & menus ✅ → world loads ✅ → lit world ✅ → gameplay starts ✅ ( 4-5 fps) → shadowed areas 🔨 → playable speed ⏳

 
 

 Donations are voluntary gifts that support development time. They are not a purchase: they buy no game content, access, builds or perks. PayPal: please send as Friends & Family (a gift).

 📸 Screenshots

All captured on an RTX 3060 under Windows 10.

 Gameplay view, lit

 

 The title's own final image in gameplay: sunlight, textures, a fence and buildings, with the movement hint on screen. Shadowed areas are still too dark and some HUD text is cut off. Built on the public VIctory fork by fxceless (GPL-3.0) with community work and our changes on top. 

 Gameplay view with stand-in lighting (earlier build)

 

 An earlier build, before the title's own lighting translated: a stand-in lighting pass (sky, a sun, fog) over the world's own geometry buffers. Fences, a bin and props are drawn; terrain and most surface colours are missing. 

 First gameplay frame (earlier build)

 

 The title's own movement hint, drawn over a still-black 3D picture because the lighting shaders did not all translate yet in that build. 

 Street, debug colours (earlier build)

 

 One of the title's own geometry buffers shown in the window with a debug colour view, in real time. Lighting and textures are not there. That view is not part of the current runtime source. 

 Interior, debug colours (earlier build)

 

 A sofa from an interior scene, drawn in real time with the same debug colour view of an internal buffer. The geometry is there; the lighting pass still output black in that build. 

 First world geometry (earlier build)

 

 One of the title's own render passes drawing the ground in 3D perspective. An internal pass, not a final image. 

 First-boot settings screen

 

 A first-boot settings screen drawn by the title on the VIctory runtime; the window caption shows 30 fps. Other screens (title artwork, loading screens, legal notices) are left out of this repo on purpose. 

---

 🧱 What blocks a good picture

Measured on an RTX 3060 (Series S profile, the title's own upscaler):

- Speed: about 4 fps while walking and turning in the world, with steady pacing (95th-percentile frame about 270 ms). That is far from 30 fps. The GPU profiler ( VICTORY GPU PROFILE ) measures about 93-111 ms of GPU time per frame, spread over about 1,100 pipelines, so no single pass is the one to fix. The intro cutscene is very slow unless it is skipped.
- Pipeline compile freezes: on a first run, moving into new areas freezes while pipelines compile. The shader prewarm and the pipeline cache shorten this on later runs.
- Hair renders too bright; shadowed areas are too dark. The screen lighting passes are fixed (their workers are on by default), but the title's ray-traced lighting and shadows do not run yet (ray tracing is off); the ray-tracing work so far is described in runtime/victory/docs/fork-ray-tracing.md .
- Not verified playable: nobody has played a session end to end.

Details: docs/STATUS.md . Plan: docs/ROADMAP.md .
Questions: docs/FAQ.md . Problems: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md .

---

 🆕 New in v0.4.2

Measured on an RTX 3060 (Series S profile): about 4 fps while walking and turning in the world, with steady pacing (95th-percentile frame about 270 ms).

- Lighting passes fixed: the screen passes have workers of their own, on by default ( VICTORY SCREEN WORKERS=0 turns them off).
- Texture reserve fix: the room kept for card copies is capped ( VICTORY CARD ROOM KEPT MB , 512 by default), so the reserve no longer takes the memory textures need.
- Load time: running from an internal SSD, the world is reached in about 212 s, against 300 s or more before.
- In-session A/B tooling: switches are compared live within one game session.
- GPU profiler ( VICTORY GPU PROFILE ): GPU time is about 93-111 ms per frame, spread over about 1,100 pipelines.
- Shader optimizer: the safe mask removes 51% of instructions offline; the in-game test is pending, so it stays off.
- Launcher 0.4.2: the Stable preset adds VICTORY FRIENDLY=1 , which leaves processor time to the desktop while the title runs.
- Known issues: hair renders too bright, ray tracing is off, and the speed is far from 30 fps.

 New in v0.4.0

Measured on an RTX 3060 (Series S profile): about 5 fps in the cell scene, about 4 fps while moving, stable frame pacing.

- Yard stutter fixed: lazy remapping of title memory plus the copy fix ( VICTORY REMAP LAZY , VICTORY MEM SUBPAGE , VICTORY COPY NOQUERY ).
- Copies cut from 286 to 84 MB per frame.
- Fast boot fixed ( VICTORY FAST BOOT ); it stays optional and off in the presets.
- In-session A/B tooling: switch variants cycled live within one game session ( VICTORY AB ), with a per-variant summary.
- Shader prewarm: shaders are translated ahead of play, so fewer compiles land mid-session.
- Launcher 0.4.0: the Stable preset uses the fx-cand4 settings above.
- Known issues: the lighting and hair look wrong (ray tracing is off); pipeline compiles freeze the picture when moving on a first run.

 🧪 Still in progress

"In testing" means built and unit-tested, waiting for A/
